C1: (1) Humanoid:MoveTo times out after 8 seconds if the goal isn't reached; MoveToFinished then fires with reached=false, and your code ignores that argument and prints "arrived" anyway. Fix: check the bool (`local reached = hum.MoveToFinished:Wait()`), and re-call MoveTo before 8 s, or move in short segments. (2) MoveTo walks in a straight line with no obstacle avoidance. Fix: use PathfindingService: `local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({AgentRadius=2, AgentHeight=5, AgentCanJump=true})`, `pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, start, goal)`, check `path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success`, then for each `path:GetWaypoints()` call MoveTo(wp.Position) (set hum.Jump if wp.Action == Jump) and wait for MoveToFinished per waypoint, which also avoids the 8 s timeout. Listen to path.Blocked to recompute, recompute periodically for a moving target, and SetNetworkOwner(nil) on the zombie's root so the server drives it smoothly.
C2: ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn defaults to true: on every respawn the PlayerGui copy is destroyed and a fresh copy is cloned from StarterGui, which re-runs the LocalScript from scratch, so its local variables reset. Fix: set ResetOnSpawn = false on that ScreenGui (the script then runs once and keeps its state), or keep the state outside the GUI, e.g. in a ModuleScript/LocalScript under StarterPlayerScripts or player attributes, and re-apply it when the GUI is rebuilt. For persistence across sessions, send the settings to the server (validated) and save them in a DataStore.
C3: Animations replicate from the client only when the client is the authority for that Animator: a LocalScript can play animations on its own character (the player owns it, and the Animator was created by the server), and those replicate to everyone. For a server-owned NPC, animations played from a client stay local; nobody else sees them. An Animator created with Instance.new on the client exists only on that client, so nothing it plays replicates. Fix: play NPC animations from a server Script (Humanoid/AnimationController -> Animator:LoadAnimation(anim):Play()), with the Animator created on the server (or let the Humanoid create it server-side). If the client triggers the wave, fire a RemoteEvent and let the server validate and play it. Purely cosmetic local-only waves can stay client-side, but then each client must play them itself.
C4: (1) A Sound parented to Workspace (or any non-positional parent like SoundService) is non-positional (2D): everyone hears it at full volume. Parent it to a Part or Attachment at the barrel position so it is 3D; clone and play a fresh sound per explosion (Debris/Ended cleanup). (2) Positional sounds attenuate by RollOffMinDistance / RollOffMaxDistance and RollOffMode. Raise RollOffMaxDistance (and RollOffMinDistance for the full-volume radius), use Linear/InverseTapered for a controlled fall-off, and raise Volume if needed. (3) Loaded only fires once when loading completes; if the sound is already loaded (IsLoaded true) before you wait, the event never fires again, so it hangs. Use `if not siren.IsLoaded then siren.Loaded:Wait() end`, or just call Play() (it plays once loaded); optionally ContentProvider:PreloadAsync. Also check the SoundId is valid/permitted, or Loaded never fires.
C5:
workspace:Raycast's direction is the full ray vector, not just a direction: a .Unit vector is only 1 stud long, so it almost never hits anything and Raycast returns nil, then `result.Instance` errors. And with no filter, the ray starts inside your own head/character and hits it. Fix:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {player.Character}
local dir = (mouseHit - head.Position).Unit * 500
local result = workspace:Raycast(head.Position, dir, params)
if result then
  print(result.Instance.Name, result.Position)
end
```
Always nil-check the result. For a real gun, also do the authoritative raycast on the server (validate origin, distance and rate) rather than trusting the client's hit.
C6: Two tweens on the same property of the same instance conflict: when a new tween on BackgroundTransparency starts, TweenService cancels the one already running on that property, so the hover tween stops mid-way; when the flash's 'back' tween finishes it restores a hardcoded value that ignores whether the mouse is still hovering, so states end up wrong (and MouseLeave can race too). Structure: keep one source of truth (state: hovered, pressed) and a single function that computes the target value from state and plays one tween on that property, cancelling/replacing the stored current tween. E.g. `local current; local function apply() local target = pressed and 0 or (hovered and 0.2 or 0.5); if current then current:Cancel() end; current = TweenService:Create(btn, TweenInfo.new(0.15), {BackgroundTransparency = target}); current:Play() end`. MouseEnter/Leave/click only change state and call apply(); after the flash, set pressed=false and apply() again. Or animate the flash on a different property/object (e.g. a UIStroke or overlay frame, or UIScale for press) so effects never fight.
